target.name: Unlimited Industries
target.founder: Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, Tara Viswanathan

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $12M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Unlimited Industries is a seed-stage housing and construction company founded by Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, and Tara Viswanathan. The valuation assessment draws on a peer set of five private-sector comparables—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Ground Control Development, ADMARES, and Hedral—with no direct public market proxies available for triangulation.

The stage-progression method provides the primary valuation anchor. Using the company's $12M total raised as a proxy for post-money seed value, application of a 2.5x multiplier to the next funding stage implies a valuation of $30M. This methodology reflects typical step-up dynamics observed in seed-to-Series A progression within construction technology. Given the limited methodological basis, the analysis supports a valuation range of $26M (low) to $34M (high), with $30M as the central estimate.

Key uncertainties constrain confidence in this range. The reliance on a single applicable method—stage progression—rather than revenue multiples or comparable transaction multiples reflects the company's early stage and likely pre-revenue or minimal-revenue status. The private-peer comp set, while relevant sectoral anchors, provides limited direct pricing signals without disclosed transaction or valuation data. Actual post-money valuation will depend materially on recent traction metrics, capital efficiency, and market conditions at the time of next fundraising.
